name: Question 13
problem:
Find the general solution of the exact differential equation

$$
(y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-\frac{1}{x})\text{d}x+(x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-\frac{1}{y})\text{d}y=0.
$$
worked_solution:
Note that the differential equation is of the form

$$
P(x,y)\text{d}x+Q(x,y)\text{d}y=0
$$

where $P(x,y)=y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-\frac{1}{x}$ and $Q(x,y)=x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-\frac{1}{y}.$

Since the equation is exact, our solution $u(x,y)$ must satisfy the following system:

$$
\frac{∂u}{∂x}=P(x,y),\,\frac{∂u}{∂y}=Q(x,y)
$$

First, we integrate $P(x,y)$ with respect to $x.$ Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(x,y) & =\int P(x,y)\,\text{d}x+f(y) \\  & =\int (y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-\frac{1}{x})\text{d}x+f(y) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)-\operatorname{ln}⁡x+f(y)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we integrate $Q(x,y)$ with respect to $y.$  Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(x,y) & =\int Q(x,y)\,\text{d}y+g(x) \\  & =\int (x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-\frac{1}{y})\text{d}y+g(x) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)-\operatorname{ln}⁡y+g(x)\end{aligned}
$$

Comparing the two solutions, we see that we must have

$$
g(x)=-\operatorname{ln}⁡x,\,f(y)=-\operatorname{ln}⁡y.
$$

Therefore, the general solution $u(x,y)=c$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)-\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =c \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy) & =c.\end{aligned}
$$

html:
Question 13
?

Find the general solution of the exact differential equation

(ycos⁡(xy)−1x)dx+(xcos⁡(xy)−1y)dy=0.

a
sin⁡(xy)−ln⁡(xy)=c
b
 cos⁡(xy)−ln⁡(xy)=c
c
 xysin⁡(xy)−ln⁡(xy)=c
d
 ycos⁡(xy)−ln⁡y=c
e
 sin⁡(xy)−ln⁡x=c
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Note that the differential equation is of the form

P(x,y)dx+Q(x,y)dy=0

where P(x,y)=ycos⁡(xy)−1x and Q(x,y)=xcos⁡(xy)−1y.

Since the equation is exact, our solution u(x,y) must satisfy the following system:

∂u∂x=P(x,y),∂u∂y=Q(x,y)

First, we integrate P(x,y) with respect to x. Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of y:

u(x,y)=∫P(x,y)dx+f(y)=∫(ycos⁡(xy)−1x)dx+f(y)=sin⁡(xy)−ln⁡x+f(y)

Next, we integrate Q(x,y) with respect to y. Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of x:

u(x,y)=∫Q(x,y)dy+g(x)=∫(xcos⁡(xy)−1y)dy+g(x)=sin⁡(xy)−ln⁡y+g(x)

Comparing the two solutions, we see that we must have

g(x)=−ln⁡x,f(y)=−ln⁡y.

Therefore, the general solution u(x,y)=c is

sin⁡(xy)−ln⁡x−ln⁡y=csin⁡(xy)−ln⁡(xy)=c.
